task: Fix the broken health check after the service endpoint was moved to a new port.

candidate_memories.content: Load balancer health checks fail because the health endpoint moved from port 8080 to port 9090 in the last deploy.
Load balancer health check config must be updated to target port 9090 and path /healthz.
Port 9090 is now dedicated to administrative endpoints including health, metrics, and profiling.
When administrative endpoints move to a dedicated port, update all infrastructure configs atomically.
The service is still serving traffic on port 8080; only the health check is broken, not the application.
The Kubernetes readiness probe uses the same health endpoint as the load balancer.
Session 4 note: the monitoring team added a Grafana panel for health check latency.
Old practice: health checks and application traffic used the same port before the admin port separation.
The metrics endpoint on port 9090 exposes Prometheus-format metrics to the monitoring system.
Session 11 note: the on-call team added a PagerDuty integration for health check alerts.
Old health guide: the /health path returned 200 OK with a simple up response.
Administrative and application traffic must be separated on different ports for security and monitoring clarity.
Session 8 note: the SRE team updated the runbook for service health check failures.
The load balancer uses a 10-second interval and 3 consecutive failures before marking a target unhealthy.
Session 6 note: the deployment pipeline was updated to run smoke tests post-deploy.
The firewall rules allow traffic on port 8080 from the load balancer; port 9090 requires an additional rule.
When adding a new admin port, update firewall rules, load balancer config, and monitoring in the same change.
Session 9 note: the health endpoint was extended with dependency health status fields.
Old deployment guide: the port 8080 was the single port for all traffic types in the original deployment.
The profiling endpoint on port 9090 requires an internal network source IP for access.
